progressionAssessment.rationale: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and eight advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and all dependent resource courses. Mathematical Methods precedes later mathematics, robotics and neural-network courses. Environmental foundations precede advanced biogeochemistry, recovery, resources and energy work.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme passes the evidence, course-content and schedule gates. It responds to the mathematical, quantitative and matter/energy interests through explicit modelling, natural-system and energy applications. It is not represented as Physics. A fundamental-physics direction cannot supply mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, statistical physics, solid-state physics, particle/nuclear physics or relativity. An experimental-physics direction cannot supply cumulative physics laboratories, instrumentation, experimental measurement or a scheduled independent physics research project. A second algorithmic/intelligent-systems route was not included because it would draw on the same mathematical generator interests while shifting further from the stated physical-science object rather than creating a separate evidence-backed choice.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both provide programming for quantitative scientific work; UCR supplies general implementation, testing and debugging rather than physics-specific computational training.
Both establish calculus, matrices and differential-equation tools for quantitative models; the external course is embedded in a physics progression.
Both directly study matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations.
UCR develops numerical solution methods for equations and differential equations; the external component provides the physics programme’s further analysis progression.
Both extend calculus beyond the introductory level; UCR includes multivariable calculus, complex functions and differential equations.
